gallery_info.title: Turn on the look gallery?
gallery_info.description:
The look gallery is a collection of looks that other people shared. You can browse them and apply one to your own card. A look changes only how a card looks, never what it does.

Your browser will contact this website, and it will see your internet address (IP address):
- `therealmcsparrow.github.io` (run by GitHub). Only the card editor contacts it, and only while the gallery is open. It loads the list of looks and their preview images.

Many looks use Google fonts. If **Load Google Fonts** is on, any browser that shows a card with such a look also contacts `fonts.googleapis.com` and `fonts.gstatic.com` (run by Google), which see the internet address too. Load Google Fonts is a separate switch. The gallery does not turn it on and does not need it.

These websites also see the usual details a browser sends, such as its type and language. They handle that under their own privacy policies. Magic Card sends nothing else: no entity names, no card settings, no Home Assistant details. It does not count or track anything.

Nothing changes until you confirm on the next screen.

gallery_confirm.title: Turn on the look gallery for everyone?
gallery_confirm.description:
This switch applies to everyone who uses this Home Assistant. Confirming turns on the look gallery only. It does not change **Load Google Fonts**. After you turn it on, reload each open dashboard so it takes effect. In a browser, refresh the page. In the Home Assistant app on an iPad or iPhone, pull down to refresh or close and reopen the app.

You can turn the gallery off at any time with the same switch. That stops the requests to `therealmcsparrow.github.io`. Requests to Google Fonts depend only on Load Google Fonts; to stop those, turn that switch off. Cards that already use a look keep their style settings either way.

theme_files_confirm.title: Let the theme editor write to /config/themes?
theme_files_confirm.description:
With **Theme files** on, administrators can use the Magic Card theme editor to create, change and delete theme files in `/config/themes`.

What the editor does:
- It only changes or deletes files it wrote itself. Those files start with the line `# Written by the Magic Card theme editor.`
- Theme files you wrote by hand, or that came from HACS or another tool, stay read-only. To change one, the editor makes a copy under a new name; the original is never touched.
- It writes only inside `/config/themes`, never `configuration.yaml`.
- After a save or delete it reloads the themes, so every dashboard sees the change.

**Disclaimer.** You turn this on at your own risk. The editor rewrites its own files completely: comments and layout you add to them by hand are not kept, and a deleted file cannot be restored by Magic Card. A broken theme can make dashboards hard to read. Make a backup of your configuration (Settings > System > Backups) before you rely on it. Magic Card Utils is provided as is, without warranty, under its licence.

You can turn Theme files off at any time with the same switch. The files already written stay where they are, and the editor becomes read-only again.
